title: Observability Probe Layer & Auto-Escalation Orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight probe layer and orchestration service that wires tracing hooks, metrics/log ingestion, and dashboard-derived SLOs into a dynamic burn-rate and auto-escalation engine. Goal: reduce noisy pages while keeping oncall latency/error awareness accurate for multi-tenant workloads. This ticket covers schema for trace enrichment, a Kafka-backed metrics pipeline consumer, SLO computation jobs, burn-rate aggregator, and configurable paging policy DSL with canary rollout support.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hook library deployed to runtime-sidecar used by inference runtime and gateway; traces include standardized fields: request_id, customer_id, model_variant, seq_len, route
Metrics pipeline consumer reads from 'telemetry.v2' topic, enriches records with trace context, and forwards normalized time-series to SLO engine within 60s
SLO engine exposes per-customer/per-route burn-rate alerts with tunable windows (5m, 30m, 6h) and integrates with PagerDuty + Slack escalation policies
Auto-escalation rules support severity-weighted deduplication and quiet-hours overrides; end-to-end tests simulate traffic spikes and show false-positive reduction >= 35% vs baseline
Runbook and dashboard tiles (latency P50/P95/P99, error-rate, burn-rate score) created in Console; rollout to 10% of tenants behind a feature flag
comments: 2026-02-16 - Spike complete: validated that extracting trace context at gRPC interceptor level adds <1ms p50 to RPC path. Prototype committed in github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-probes/pull/24.

2026-02-22 - Design review with PM and Observability ENG: agreed on unified field names (trace.request_id, trace.customer_id, trace.model_variant). Decision: do not include full prompt text in telemetry by default; only hashed prompt fingerprint for privacy.

2026-03-01 - Engineering standup: opted for Kafka consumer approach (consumer group 'slo-ingester') to enable backpressure and replay. Metrics normalized to Prometheus-style labels before aggregation.
2026-03-04 - Privacy/security note from Compliance: KMS wrap required for any persisted customer_id values in long-term storage. Follow-up task created (ENG-880160).
2026-03-08 - Early anomaly detector integrated: lightweight z-score windowed detector for burn-rate anomalies; ML-based detector deferred to a follow-up (PM backlog).
2026-03-10 - Preparing canary: feature-flag gating implemented; will enable for internal tenants and two pilot customers next week. Ops runbook drafted (Drive link in links).
notes: Trade-off: tuned anomaly detector for lower sensitivity to avoid pager fatigue; this increases time-to-detect some regressions — mitigation: faster manual bump path and synthetic probes
Avoid storing raw prompts: use one-way fingerprint and token-length histogram to preserve signal for quality regressions without exposing data
Will instrument both hosted API and dedicated nodes; private deployments will expose same hooks but telemetry forwarding is opt-in for air-gapped customers
Follow-up work: ML-based anomaly scorer (ENG-881501), richer deduplication heuristics (ENG-882020), and UI for per-tenant paging tuning
